perf.summary: Per-sample full-mesh distance scan recomputes per-triangle invariants (edge vectors and the barycentric denominator) every call.
perf.currentCost: In BuildPolyDetail the sample-error loop (lines 1452-1478) calls DistToTriMesh for every un-added sample on every iteration (O(nsamples^2) overall), and DistToTriMesh loops over all ntris calling DistPtTri. DistPtTri recomputes v0=c-a, v1=b-a, dot00,dot01,dot11 and invDenom = 1/((dot00*dot11)-(dot01*dot01)) for the same triangle on every sample query, including a divide per triangle per sample.
perf.proposedChange: When the triangulation is stable across the inner sample scan, precompute per-triangle (a, v0, v1, dot00, dot01, dot11, invDenom) once into a small stackalloc/Temp cache after each DelaunayHull rebuild, and have the inner DistPtTri only compute v2=p-a, dot02, dot12, the two barycentric coords and the y interpolation. Mark VDot2 AggressiveInlining.
perf.rationale: Moves ~3 dot products and one division per (triangle,sample) pair to per-triangle-once, turning the dominant inner cost from ~5 dots+1 div to ~2 dots. Given the nsamples x ntris x (per-iter) nesting this is the largest constant-factor win in the detail-mesh build and removes a divide from the innermost loop.
perf.risk: Cache must be invalidated whenever tris changes (after each DelaunayHull rebuild at line 1500 and the initial TriangulateHull). invDenom hoist is bit-identical (same operands, same order). The clamp/eps tests are unchanged. Watch maxTris (255) so the cache buffer is bounded; allocate for maxTris triangles.

perf.summary: TriangulateHull compares triangle perimeters using VDist2 (sqrt) where squared lengths would suffice for ordering, and recomputes shared edge lengths.
perf.currentCost: VDist2 calls math.sqrt (lines 306-309). In the perimeter heuristic (line 1160 ear selection, and 1190-1191 left/right advance) only relative comparisons of perimeter sums are needed, yet each VDist2 pays a sqrt. The advance loop runs O(nhull) times with 4 sqrt calls per iteration; the ear selection adds 3 sqrt per hull vertex.
perf.proposedChange: Where the value is only used in a comparison (dleft<dright, d<dmin), the sum-of-sqrt is not equal to sqrt-of-sum so you cannot trivially drop sqrt on a *sum*; instead cache VDist2 results for shared edges between consecutive iterations (e.g. VDist2(cvleft,nvleft) reused as the new edge next step) and reuse the previously computed cvleft/cvright endpoints to avoid recomputing one of the two terms each advance.
perf.rationale: Each advance step shares an endpoint with the previous one; caching the one overlapping distance removes ~1 of the ~4 sqrt evaluations per iteration of the hull walk, a direct reduction in transcendental ops on a per-poly path.
perf.risk: Because the heuristic sums two sqrt values, you cannot replace with squared distances without changing which branch is taken; do NOT do that. Only the caching/reuse of identical VDist2(endpointA,endpointB) values is safe and bit-exact. Verify the reused pair truly matches operand order (VDist2 is symmetric, so order is irrelevant).

perf.summary: Per-sample point-in-polygon + edge-distance test recomputes edge-derived divisions every call though the polygon (@in) is fixed for the whole sample grid.
perf.currentCost: DistToPoly is called once per grid sample (line 1425) over the same nin-vertex polygon. Each call, for each edge, computes (vj[0]-vi[0]) and divides by (vj[2]-vi[2]) for the crossing test, and calls DistancePtSeg2d which recomputes pqx,pqz,d per edge. All edge-intrinsic terms (dx, dz, 1/d, the crossing slope) are invariant across samples.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist a per-edge precompute (edge dx, dz, invLen2 = d>0?1/d:0, and slope (vj[0]-vi[0])/(vj[2]-vi[2]) guarded for horizontal edges) into a small stackalloc cache built once before the sample double-loop in BuildPolyDetail, and pass it to a specialized DistToPoly that only does the per-sample dot/clamp.
perf.rationale: Turns O(samples*edges) divisions into O(edges) divisions plus O(samples*edges) multiplies, removing a division from the innermost grid-sample test. The sample grid can be large (bbox/sampleDist in x and z), so this scales with sample count.
perf.risk: The crossing test uses an exact comparison with a divided slope; precomputing slope changes the order of the division relative to the multiply by (p[2]-vi[2]), which can alter the last ULP and flip the inside/outside classification for points exactly on an edge. Keep the crossing-test arithmetic in its original form/order and only hoist the DistancePtSeg2d edge invariants (dx,dz,d) which are used for a min and are far less tie-sensitive. Stated guard: do not reassociate the slope division if exact boundary classification must match.
